# Text drawn in graphics (pt-BR redraw)

Status of the picture work (branch main, 2026-10-16). The pt-BR pictures are patches on the *decoded* game data, applied by the engine only when the
language is pt-BR; English is byte-identical (the patch is looked up by the hash of the decoded original, a missing / foreign patch leaves the picture).

## How it works
* `i18n/pt-BR/gfx.tsv` (committed, generated by `python3 scripts/gfx_i18n/make_patch.py` from the user's `assets/raw`; no original picture is stored, only the
  redrawn bytes): `blob <DATA file> <sub address> <fnv64 of the decoded original> <decoded length> <offset> <new bytes>` (runs of changed bytes of an LZKN1 blob after
  decoding; a run beyond the end grows the blob, at most 0x2000 bytes) and `file <DATA file> <offset> <original bytes> <new bytes>` (raw bytes of a DATA file: sprite
  frame sizes, typing delays, frame offsets; an empty original = append at the end of the file, used for the new caption frames).
* `snt i18n-build` puts the patch in the pack (optional trailing section, `core/src/gfxpatch.rs`); `snt i18n-gfx-check i18n/pt-BR assets/raw` verifies every blob
  hash / length and every original byte against the user's disc files (0 failures expected); `snt i18n-gfx-info i18n/pt-BR` lists the patch.
* Engine: `SubMem::decomp` (core/src/gfx.rs) decodes every picture blob (scene VRAM lists and tile channels) and applies the patch while the language is pt-BR
  (`Engine::sync_gfx`); `DATA` files get their raw patches when loaded (`cmd_load`). A scene already on screen keeps its pictures until it is loaded again.
* Tools (all dev only, read `assets/raw`): `scripts/gfx_i18n/` (`data.py` DATA reader, `planes.py` plane picture re-tiler, `textfont.py` TTF text with the grey levels of
  the pictures, `bmfont.py` / `skelfont.py` / `vpfont.py` pixel fonts cut from the originals, one module per item, `make_patch.py`), `engine/examples/run`
  (`GFXTRACE=1`, `SPRTILES=1`, `VRAMDUMP`, `CRAMDUMP`, `OBJDUMP`), `scripts/gfx_i18n/runshot.sh` (before / after PNGs in `work/i18n/gfx/shots/`).

## Kept in English (and why)
* **NO DATA** (slot screen): the cells of the play time / NO DATA text are written at run time (the module draws the panel into Word RAM), a patch of the blobs behind them leaked into the play time digits (tried, reverted). **SNATCHER n** names stay (title).
* **Options screen** (OPTIONS, DEVICE, JOYPAD ONLY, CONTROLS + the six button-configuration variants, SOUND MODE, STEREO / MONO, GUN ADJUST, QUIT): drawn from many state-dependent tile lists (selected row yellow / grey, values toggled at run time); each state would need its own patch of tiles and nametable rows, not attempted. Short, technical, and the pt-BR player sees the button letters anyway.
* **Dec. 2047 / NEO KOBE CITY** (prologue): the text is on a plane the dump of the finished screen does not show consistently (64 cell planes with scroll); NEO KOBE CITY is a name and only "Dec." would become "Dez.", so it stays.
* **Neo Kobe Times front page headlines** (MYSTERIOUS LIFE-FORM, PLANE CRASH DEATH REACH 55?, ...): halftone / dithered newspaper print, not a font; a clean redraw would look different from the page. Masthead and article text stay.
* **SP09 file pages** (Metal Gear reads them aloud, clips 221-235): kept English. The pages are 15 full-screen pictures of dense small text with portraits and layout; the pt-BR voice subtitle already shows the reading below the picture (compact band), so the player gets the content; redrawing about 15 screens of text would be most of the job for little gain, and the reading is voice-driven.
* Backup RAM error screens (DATA_D2 scenes 1-6), GUN ADJUST title, SNATCHER and KONAMI logos, copyright / legal lines, staff roll and cast, posters / signs in rooms: out of scope or not reachable.

## Checks
`cargo test --release -p snengine --test gfx_i18n` (English identical with / without the pack, pt-BR blobs patched only in pt-BR), `core/src/gfxpatch.rs` unit tests (round trip, growth, append),
`tools` test `tsv_round_trips_into_the_pack_patch`, `snt i18n-gfx-check i18n/pt-BR assets/raw`. A whole boot / intro run in both languages (12400 frames, a frame every 100) differs only on the
frames of the translated pictures (title, disclaimer, RSS, dedication, Moscow, 50 years).
Before / after images (3-5x): `work/i18n/gfx/shots/cmp_*.png` (gitignored), e.g. `cmp_title_f001180`, `cmp_act2_f000100`, `cmp_cap_f000930`, `cmp_vp2_f000100`, `cmp_slot_f001500`, `cmp_go_f000300`, `cmp_japan_f011070`, `cmp_ded_f003500`, `cmp_disc_f001900`, `cmp_moscow_f003900`.

## Intro / prologue (DATA_D1, DATA_D0)
Scenes rendered with the prologue timeline (`timeline.rs`): "Moscow: June 6, 1996", the corridor, the DNA screens, the Neo Kobe Times front page,
the SNATCHER logo, JAPAN, "Dec. 2047 NEO KOBE CITY". All are pictures. The Neo Kobe Times page is a full newspaper with article text.

## Act cards and location captions (ACT 1 [`act1`], Omni Building [`omni_building`, `omni_caption`])
* The "ACT 1 / SNATCH" card and the next act cards are pictures (DATA file of the act intro; to verify).
* The typed location captions ("Konami Omni Building", "Junker Headquarters", ...) are drawn letter by letter in a serif face by the scene
  code; the letters come from a picture tile set, not from the message font, so they cannot be translated by the pack.

## In-game pictures with legible text (to verify one by one in the viewer)
* **SP09 file reading** (script label L_0ff4, silent replay L_10e9): Metal Gear reads an investigation file aloud on a framed screen; the pages are pictures drawn by the animation objects 0x14..0x1c of DATA_G0 (no script string), shown while the voice clips 221-235 (2.1 min) play. English only (docs/voice-inventory.md).
* GAME OVER picture and the videophone not-in-service / no-video banners (SP18, SP35): graphics that go with voice clips 48, 1193, 1191.
* GAME OVER picture (shown at state 4, then the game restarts at the title: `Engine::reset_to_title`).
* Staff roll of the ending (DATA_Y16): the credit lines are tile text (names, job titles in English/Japanese romanisation).
* Posters, signs and screens inside the room scenes (hospital neon "OLEEN", Konami posters, shop signs, newspaper headlines). They matter for
  puzzle text only where the dialogue reads them aloud ("Oleen Hospital", "Queens"); those readings are translated in the script.
* Jordan / patient-record screens use the message font, so they are translated.

## What stays English on purpose (not graphics, but listed here so nobody hunts for it)
* Typed-name and keyboard entry menus (SP05 name entry, Napoleon password words, SP09 birthmark answers, SP18 numbers): the engine compares
  typed or selected English text with the game's English answers, so those labels cannot be changed without changing logic.
* Letters of the on-screen keyboard and the word START printed by the controller icon patch.
* Intentionally untranslated strings: 8 in SP02 (song lyrics, a Japanese greeting, silence dots), the JUNKER/JORDAN acronym expansions, the
  "Face to face" memo, "liquid sky" / SNOW-9 / Junker's Eye (names), and the SP01 developer debug menu (see docs/i18n.md).

## How to redraw later
1. Locate the tile set with the asset viewer (palette + tile sheet of the scene chunk).
2. Redraw into the same tile budget (tiles are 8x8, 4 bpp, the scene palette applies) and re-encode with the LZKN1 tool (`snt lzkn-d` is the
   decoder; an encoder is needed or the blob can be stored uncompressed if the loader allows it).
3. Ship it as an overlay patch loaded only when the language is pt-BR, the same way the string pack works (engine side: a per-scene asset
   substitution table). Keep the English picture as default.
